topic: PCSO FY2027 budget, programs, and charitable mandate
summary: PCSO presented its FY2027 priorities as expanding medical assistance, transport, equipment donations, coastal access, cancer care, digital services, and revenue generation under its charitable mandate. It reported about 8.13 billion in medical assistance from 2024 through the first semester of 2026 and estimated 2027 retail receipts at about 68.55 billion, with 20,150,000,000 identified for the charity fund. Jan Rurik Padiernos asked about the legal and operational feasibility of landing craft vessels and about equitable deployment of ambulances and AI-capable X-rays. General Manager Mel Robles said PCSO would initially procure around 10 vessels for provincial governments, with bidder maintenance and training for three years, and would use need, priority, personnel capacity, and request order in distributing equipment. Members broadly manifested support for the PCSO budget, while Robles indicated that a second round of ambulances and continued outpatient consultation would be pursued. The precise LCV budget allocation and several garbled financial figures remained unspecified.
question: The committee was examining PCSO's proposed FY2027 programs and the resources needed to carry out its charitable mandate, including medical assistance, transport, equipment, remittances, and revenue allocation. Members also sought clarification on the feasibility and intended beneficiaries of landing craft vessels, ambulances, and AI-capable X-ray machines.
agency_position: PCSO maintained that its proposed FY2027 programs were necessary to expand health assistance, medical transport, equipment donations, coastal access, revenue generation, and efficient service delivery under its charitable mandate. It defended the LCV initiative as a medical-mobility program for coastal communities, with an initial procurement of around 10 vessels, provincial-government implementation, and three years of bidder-provided maintenance and training.
outcome: PCSO's programs and charitable mandate were presented without substantive opposition, and members broadly expressed support for the proposed 2027 budget. Questions on LCV procurement, allocation criteria, and expanded ambulance assistance were answered at a general level, with implementation details and the LCV budget allocation not fully specified.

thread.speaker: Judge Felix Piraeus, PCSO official
thread.said: He presented PCSO's proposed budget and programs and reaffirmed its mandate under Republic Act No. Eleven sixty nine, as amended, to generate and provide funds for health programs, medical assistance and services, and charitable activities of national character.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: She identified PCSO's 2027 priorities as distributing landing craft vessels to coastal provinces and municipalities, donating medical equipment, participating in a radiation oncology center, developing new games and betting platforms, and digitalizing operations.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: She reported that from 2024 through the first semester of 2026, PCSO provided 8,130,000,000 in medical assistance to 681,099 beneficiaries. The transcript states that 2024 assistance was 240,000,000 for 326,482 beneficiaries and that 2025 assistance increased to an unclear amount despite beneficiaries declining to 236,217.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: She said PCSO had expanded financial assistance to include professional fees for qualified patients, following the expressed desire of House appropriations members.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: Institutional partnership beneficiaries increased from 19 in 2024 to 38 in 2025, while assistance increased from 12,000,000 to 24,600,000; another 19 beneficiaries had been assisted by the first semester of 2026.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: Medical transport vehicle beneficiaries increased from four thirty one in 2024 to ten ninety in 2025, while assistance increased from 913,700,000 to 2,480,000,000. As of 07/31/2026, PCSO had distributed 154 PTVs.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: Medical equipment assistance increased from 20,500,000 in 2024 to 22,000,000 in 2025 and reached 154,580,000 in the first semester of 2026. Outpatient and multispecialty clinic beneficiaries were 7,383 in 2024, 9,416 in 2025, and 8,440 in the first half of 2026.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: Total revenues from major games increased by 4.02 from 62,350,000,000 in 2024 to 64,860,000,000 in 2025. STL increased by 11.99% and the National Instant Sweep Stakes program by 20%; the first-semester 2026 revenue figure was stated only as 'billion' and is unclear.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: Total income increased from 63,420,000,000 in 2024 to 65,870,000,000 in 2025, while operating expenses rose from 51,010,000,000 to 53,860,000,000. Profit after tax declined from PHP11.74 billion to PHP11.52 billion, and financial assistance, subsidies and contributions rose from 7,890,000,000 to 9,540,000,000.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: Net income decreased from 3,840,000,000 in 2024 to 1,980,000,000 in 2025. As of 06/30/2026, PCSO had recorded 31,740,000,000 in total income and PHP 3,350,000,000 in net income.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: For 2023, retail receipts were 61,460,000,000, with 33,220,000,000 allocated to the price fund, 18.11% to the charity fund, and 9,050,000,000 to the operating fund. For 2024, net receipts were PHP 61,300,000,000, with PHP 33,710,000,000 for the price fund, PHP18.39 billion for the charity fund, and PHP9.19 billion for the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: For 2025, the transcript states retail receipts of 4,860,000,000, printing cost of 1.09, and net receipts of 63,770,000,000. Allocations were 35,070,000,000 to the price fund, PHP19.13 billion to the charity fund, and PHP9.57 billion to the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: For 2026, estimated retail receipts were 67,260,000,000 and projected net receipts were stated as NT65.91 billion dollars. The estimated allocations were PHP36.25 billion to the price fund, PHP19.77 billion to the charity fund, and PHP9.89 billion to the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: For 2027, estimated retail receipts were PHP 68,550,000,000. Projected net receipts were stated as TWD67.18 billion, and the allocations were stated as 5% or RMB39.95 billion for the price fund, 30% or 20,150,000,000 for the charity fund, and 15% or 10,080,000,000 for the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: PCSO exceeded its 2025 target of 500 patient transport vehicles by distributing ten ninety PTVs, or 218% of target. For 2026, the target was two fifty eight PTVs, of which 154 had been distributed as of 07/31/2026.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: The 2025 medical assistance target was 3,302,000,000, of which 3,245,000,000 was released to 236,217 patients. For 2026, PCSO allocated 3,650,000,000 and had released 1,640,000,000 to 118,400 patients as of 06/30/2026.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: PCSO reported that portable AI-capable X-ray machines and other medical equipment donated to beneficiary entities amounted to 176,000,000. Charitimba, mobility aids, assistive devices, rescue devices, and evacuation kits distributed under the corporate social responsibility program amounted to 348,600,000.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: PCSO remitted approximately 570,000,000 under the universal health care program for 2025. For 2026, first-quarter remittances were 651,470,000 and second-quarter remittances were 690,670,000; the transcript states a combined amount due and remitted of 3,914,000,000 pesos.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong, PCSO official
thread.said: She reported that PCSO's total contributions to the National Treasury increased from 14,560,000,000 in 2021 to 21,850,000,000 in 2025. The transcript gives the five-year total and tax amount only as 'billion,' which is unclear, and states dividends of PHP9.93 billion and Universal Healthcare contributions of PHP9.53 billion.

thread.speaker: Attorney Anna Lisa, PCSO official
thread.said: As of 06/30/2026, PCSO had remitted an additional 11,060,000,000, bringing total contributions reflected in the table to 112,350,000,000.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: He questioned the procurement and feasibility of landing craft vessels as a FY2027 strategic thrust, including PCSO's legal mandate, procurement of naval vessels, and the total 2027 budget allocation. The amount sought was not clearly stated in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: He answered that the vessels would operate within municipal islands or coastal areas to provide medical mobility and serve as a 'door to door hospital.' PCSO would begin with around 10 procurements, with provincial governments receiving responsibility for scheduling and maintenance; the winning bidder would maintain each vessel for the first three years and train personnel.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: He asked about equity in the distribution of patient transport vehicles and deployment of AI-capable portable X-rays, citing the reported distribution of sixteen seventy five units, around 730,000,000, and 197,000,000 worth of medical equipment. He asked what criteria PCSO used for geographically isolated, disadvantaged, or urbanized LGUs.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: He said beneficiary LGUs needed personnel who could administer the service and work with the equipment, including radiologist specialization for the X-ray machines. Selection combined priority, demonstrated need, ability to train personnel, and a first-come, first-served order of requests.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: He manifested his full support for PCSO's proposed budget and urged PCSO to continue its programs. He also said the House of Representatives would assist as it could to help more people.

thread.speaker: Representative Ramil Hernandez
thread.said: He congratulated PCSO and expressed full support for its proposed 2027 budget.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: He expressed full support for the budget.

thread.speaker: Representative Christie Gonzales
thread.said: She thanked PCSO for hospitalization and medical assistance, including support when congressional offices had limited guarantee letters, and expressed full support for PCSO's budget request.

thread.speaker: Representative Presley de Jesus
thread.said: As deputy minority leader, he said the minority would support PCSO 100% during plenary budget proceedings and that he would not ask questions in plenary.

thread.speaker: Representative Christie Gonzales
thread.said: She raised the need for additional ambulances for a densely populated city and referred to PCSO's combination of first-come, first-served selection and LGU willingness.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: He said ambulances are emergency vehicles and that one of PCSO's next aspirations was to provide a second round and immediate standby ambulances. He told offices to call PCSO so assistance could be provided.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: He said PCSO had an outpatient clinic and would continue providing free consultation, subject to availability.

thread.speaker: Representative Christie Gonzales
thread.said: She said she would announce the outpatient clinic program through her Facebook program and fully supported all PCSO programs.

thread.speaker: Representative Mia Ynares
thread.said: She thanked PCSO for supporting Rizal province but noted that her district had not received the highlighted assistance apart from charity assistance. She asked PCSO not to forget her district.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: He said Rizal was the first province to achieve 100% distribution of patient transport vehicles or ambulances and indicated that a second round would be pursued.

topic: PhilHealth UHC remittances and 40% net charity fund share
summary: PCSO reported approximately 570 million in UHC remittances for 2025, followed by 651.47 million and 690.67 million for the first and second quarters of 2026. It said the combined amount due and remitted was 3.914 billion pesos and that each period reflected 100% remittance. Rep. Montez asked whether the legally required 40% net charity fund share had been remitted quarterly and on time. A PCSO official answered that remittances were timely and quarterly, with no remembered instances of delay, and said the general manager had personally delivered the latest remittance to the National Treasury. Rep. Montez cited a July 16 turnover of 1.935 billion covering mandatory contributions from the fourth quarter of 2025 through the first and second quarters of 2026. She requested official remittance records so they could be checked against DOF, DBM, and PhilHealth data, and PCSO committed to submit them.
question: The committee was trying to establish whether PCSO had remitted the legally required 40% of its net charity fund share for PhilHealth's Universal Health Care program on a quarterly basis. It also sought official PCSO records that could be compared with remittance data from the National Treasury, the Department of Finance, and the DBM.
agency_position: PCSO stated that it had remitted the amounts due under the UHC program in full and on time each quarter, with the amount due matching the amount remitted for each period. It committed to submit official Bureau of the Treasury remittance records covering the 40% net charity fund share for committee verification.
outcome: PCSO asserted that its UHC remittances were complete, quarterly, and timely, but the committee required documentary verification. The issue remained open pending submission of PCSO's official remittance records and comparison with DOF, DBM, and PhilHealth data.

positions.position: She indicated that PCSO appeared to have made its remittances on time, but said she still needed to compare PCSO's records with information from the DBM, DOF, and PhilHealth to determine whether any broader remittance problem existed.

topic: PCSO remittances to the Philippine Sports Commission
summary: Rep. Faustino Michael D. raised the Supreme Court ruling requiring PCSO to remit 30% of charity fund proceeds from six draws per year, including lotto, beginning in 2006. He questioned why PCSO's reported 2025 payment was only 1,500,000 and asked for the exact amount owed, the amount already remitted, and a settlement schedule. A PCSO official discussed the applicable six-digit game mechanics and cited 45,000,000, more or less 73,000,000 for remittances from 2006 to 2025, and other conflicting figures including 122,000,419 and 122,000,000,000. The exchange also referred to a 5% calculation tied to races or draws, without reconciling it with the member's cited 30% obligation. No payment schedule or documentary accounting was committed on the record, leaving the issue unresolved.
question: The committee sought to establish whether PCSO had complied with the Supreme Court ruling requiring remittance to the Philippine Sports Commission of 30% of the charity fund proceeds from six draws per year, including lotto, from 2006 onward. It also sought the exact accumulated amount owed, the amount already remitted, and the schedule for settling any balance.
agency_position: PCSO officials stated that remittances to the Philippine Sports Commission were calculated using a percentage tied to the number of races or draws for the six-digit games. They cited remittances of more or less 73,000,000 for 2006 to 2025 and also referred to a total of 122,000,419 and 122,000,000,000, but the figures and their units were inconsistent or unclear in the transcript.
outcome: PCSO provided partial and internally unclear figures on remittances, but did not clearly establish compliance with the cited 30% requirement, the exact accumulated balance, or a schedule for settling any shortfall. The issue remained contested and unresolved.

positions.position: He questioned PCSO's compliance with the Supreme Court ruling, considered the reported 1,500,000 2025 remittance insufficient, and sought an exact accounting of the amount due, the amount remitted, and the settlement schedule.

topic: Landing craft vessels, patient transport, and AI-capable X-rays
summary: Jan Rurik Padiernos asked PCSO about the legal basis and feasibility of procuring landing craft vessels for coastal provinces and municipalities. PCSO general manager Mel Robles said the vessels would support medical mobility, begin with around 10 procurements, be provided to provincial governments, and be maintained by the winning bidder for the first three years, including personnel training. Pajernos also cited 1,675 patient transport vehicles at around 730,000,000 and 197,000,000 in medical equipment, including AI-capable portable X-rays, and asked about equitable deployment. Robles said distribution considered need, priority, personnel and training capacity, and the order of requests, with a first-come, first-served element. Members broadly supported PCSO’s proposed budget and programs. PCSO also indicated that a second round of ambulances and standby support was an aspiration, while Robles said Rizal had already achieved 100% distribution of patient transport vehicles.
question: The committee sought to establish PCSO’s legal mandate and procurement plans for landing craft vessels, including their intended recipients, maintenance, and feasibility. It also sought the proposed allocations and distribution criteria for patient transport vehicles, ambulances, and AI-capable portable X-rays, particularly for geographically isolated or disadvantaged areas and urbanized LGUs.
agency_position: PCSO said the landing craft vessel initiative fell within its medical-mobility and charitable-services mandate, with provincial governments responsible for scheduling and maintenance, subject to Marina licensing. It said patient transport and AI-capable X-ray distribution depended on need and priority, the LGU’s ability to provide and train personnel, and the order of requests, including a first-come, first-served element.
outcome: PCSO answered the questions on intended use, provincial-government responsibility, licensing, contractor maintenance, and distribution criteria. The members expressed broad support, while the timing and scope of the second round of ambulances and the detailed legal and budget basis for the landing craft vessels were not further documented.

positions.position: Supported PCSO’s proposed budget and sought assurance that specialized assets would be procured and distributed under a lawful, feasible, and equitable framework.
Expressed full support for PCSO’s proposed 2027 budget.
Supported PCSO’s budget and programs and emphasized the value of its hospitalization assistance, MIPS, and patient transport support.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Jan Rurik Padiernos asked PCSO about the procurement and feasibility of landing craft vessels under the fiscal year 2027 strategy, including whether PCSO had the legal mandate to procure such heavy maritime assets for coastal provinces and municipalities.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Mel Robles said the vessels would operate within municipal islands or the relevant area. He linked the initiative to PCSO’s mandate to provide medical mobility and charity services of national character, with the intention of creating a “door to door hospital” service.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Robles said LGUs would need to secure licenses from Marina after receiving the vessels. He said PCSO was starting with around 10 procurements and would proceed from there in the next year.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Robles clarified that the landing craft vessels would be provided to provincial governments, which would schedule and maintain them. The winning bidder would be required to maintain each vessel for the first three years and train the personnel.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Pajernos asked about equity in the distribution of patient transport vehicles and the deployment of AI-capable portable X-rays. He cited a report that PCSO planned 100% distribution of patient transport vehicles, 1,675 units at around 730,000,000, and 197,000,000 worth of medical equipment, including AI-capable portable X-rays.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Pajernos asked whether PCSO’s criteria prioritized geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas or urbanized LGUs, and sought the basis for determining the number and order of deployments.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Robles said PCSO considered whether the LGU had personnel who could provide the services and operate the equipment, including personnel with radiologist specialization. The LGU also had to demonstrate that it could administer the service.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Robles said allocation was based on a combination of need, priority, the LGU’s ability to train personnel to handle the equipment, and the order of requests. He also described the process as first come, first served.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Pajernos said he was making a manifestation of full support for PCSO’s proposed budget and hoped PCSO would continue its work for the country. He said the House of Representatives would assist as much as possible to help more people.

thread.speaker: Representative Ramil Hernandez
thread.said: Representative Ramil Hernandez congratulated PCSO for its work and expressed full support for its proposed 2027 budget.

thread.speaker: Representative Christie Gonzales
thread.said: Representative Christie Gonzales thanked PCSO for its financial assistance for hospitalization and MIPS and expressed full support for PCSO’s budget request.

thread.speaker: Representative Presley de Jesus
thread.said: Representative Presley de Jesus expressed support for PCSO and said that, as deputy minority leader, he would not ask questions during plenary budget deliberations and would support PCSO 100 on behalf of the minority.

thread.speaker: Representative Christie Gonzales
thread.said: Gonzales thanked PCSO for its support and referred to the patient transport vehicle distribution as a blend of first come, first served and the willingness and capacity of the LGU. She noted the relevance of the criteria to a densely populated city and its need for ambulances.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Robles described ambulances as emergency vehicles and said one of PCSO’s next aspirations was to provide a second round and an immediate standby ambulance. He said offices could call PCSO for assistance.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Robles said PCSO also had an outpatient clinic office available to provide services, including free consultation, subject to availability.

thread.speaker: Representative Mia Ynares
thread.said: Representative Mia Ynares thanked PCSO for supporting Rizal province but said her district had not received the referenced equipment or vehicles, except for charity assistance. She asked PCSO not to forget her district.

thread.speaker: Mel Robles, PCSO general manager
thread.said: Robles said Rizal was the first province to achieve 100% distribution of patient transport vehicles or ambulances, possibly before Ynares took office. He added that she should not worry because a second round would follow.

topic: Ambulance assistance and equitable district medical assistance
summary: PCSO reported that its medical transport vehicle program had grown substantially, including 154 PTVs distributed as of 07/31/2026 and performance of 218% against the 2025 target. Representative Christie Gonzales raised the need for more equitable coverage for densely populated Mandaluyong and additional ambulances. GM Mel Robles said PCSO's next aspiration was a second round of ambulance distribution and offered immediate standby ambulances upon request. Representative Mia Ynares said Rizal province had received strong support but that her district had not received the assistance under discussion. PCSO said Rizal had achieved 100% patient transport vehicle distribution and reiterated the prospect of a second round, but did not give a schedule or specific district allocation.
question: The committee was trying to establish how PCSO distributed patient transport vehicles and whether districts with dense populations or insufficient ambulance coverage could receive additional vehicles. Members also sought clarification on whether PCSO would undertake a second round of ambulance distribution and provide immediate standby assistance.
agency_position: PCSO stated that it had substantially expanded patient transport vehicle distribution and had completed or was pursuing distribution across provinces, cities and municipalities. Its general manager said PCSO aspired to conduct a second round of ambulance distribution and could provide an immediate standby ambulance when an office called.
outcome: PCSO defended its broad PTV distribution and acknowledged requests for denser district coverage and additional ambulances. A second round and standby assistance were indicated, but no timetable, allocation criteria, or specific commitment to Representative Ynares's district was stated.

positions.position: Supported PCSO but sought more equitable ambulance coverage for Mandaluyong, citing its dense population and need for additional ambulances.
Expressed gratitude for PCSO's support to Rizal province but said her district had not received the assistance under discussion and asked not to be forgotten.

topic: PCSO sales, taxes, dividends, and special-law remittances
summary: PCSO presented rising sales and net-receipt estimates, from about 61.46 billion in 2023 to about 68.55 billion in projected 2027 retail receipts. It reported UHC remittances, including about 570 million in 2025 and 651.47 million and 690.67 million in the first two quarters of 2026, and said amounts due and remitted matched. The agency also reported total contributions rising from 14.56 billion in 2021 to 21.85 billion in 2025, with an additional 11.06 billion remitted by June 2026 and a table total of 112.35 billion. Chair Mika Swan Singh questioned why taxes, dividends, and other remittances appeared to decline or remain flat despite rising sales. PCSO's accounting and budget official attributed the pattern to corporate income, final income, and winnings-related taxes, income-based dividends, sales-related UHC and DST computations, and contingent special-law obligations. The chair accepted the explanation, commended PCSO's contributions, and left the matter informational.
question: The committee sought to establish why PCSO sales and projected revenues were rising while taxes, dividends, and other statutory remittances appeared flat or declining. It also asked whether the decline in remittances under Republic Acts and executive orders reflected specific laws or factors outside PCSO's control.
agency_position: PCSO stated that taxes and dividends were driven principally by corporate income, final income, and winnings-related taxes, while some special-law contributions depended on sales and other contingent factors. It maintained that UHC remittances were fully remitted for the periods reflected and emphasized its significant overall contribution to government revenues and national programs.
outcome: PCSO explained that the differing trajectories reflected the separate statutory and financial bases of taxes, dividends, UHC, and special-law contributions. The chair acknowledged the explanation and commended PCSO; no document request or further undertaking was recorded.

positions.position: Sales and revenues should generally produce a corresponding increase in taxes, dividends, and other government contributions, although she accepted that some remittances were contingent on factors outside PCSO's control.

positions.who: Johann, PCSO accounting and budget department
positions.position: The differing trajectories were explained by the specific bases of each remittance: corporate income and winnings-related taxes, net income for dividends, sales-related computations for UHC and DST, and contingent special-law obligations.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: PCSO reported that total revenues from major games increased by 4.02 from 62,350,000,000 in 2024 to 64,860,000,000 in 2025. The increase was attributed mainly to STL, which grew by 11.99%, and the National Instant Sweep Stakes program, which grew by 20%; the first-semester 2026 revenue figure was stated only as “billion.”

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: For 2023, PCSO reported 61,460,000,000 in retail receipts from Lotto, STL and NISP, with 55% or 33,220,000,000 allocated to the price fund, 30% or 18.11% to the charity fund, and 15% or 9,050,000,000 to the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: For 2024, retail receipts were 62,350,000,000. After deducting 1,060,000,000 in printing costs, net receipts were PHP 61,300,000,000; allocations were 55% or PHP 33,710,000,000 to the price fund, 30% or PHP18.39 billion to the charity fund, and 15% or PHP9.19 billion to the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: For 2025, PCSO reported 4,860,000,000 in retail receipts from Lotto, STL and NISP after deducting 1.09 in printing cost. Net receipts were 63,770,000,000, with 55% or 35,070,000,000 for the price fund, 30% or PHP19.13 billion for the charity fund, and 15% or PHP9.57 billion for the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: For 2026, estimated retail receipts were 67,260,000,000. After deducting the estimated “billion dollars” for printing cost, projected net receipts were NT65.91 billion, with PHP36.25 billion for the price fund, PHP19.77 billion for the charity fund, and PHP9.89 billion for the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: For 2027, estimated retail receipts were PHP 68,550,000,000. After deducting the estimated billion for printing costs, projected net receipts were TWD67.18 billion; the stated allocations were 5% or RMB39.95 billion for the price fund, 30% or 20,150,000,000 for the charity fund, and 15% or 10,080,000,000 for the operating fund.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: PCSO reported that it remitted approximately 570,000,000 under the Universal Health Care program in 2025. For 2026, the first-quarter remittance was 651,470,000 and the second-quarter remittance was 690,670,000.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: PCSO stated that combined 2025 and first-semester 2026 UHC amounts due and remitted totaled 3,914,000,000 pesos. It said the amounts due and remitted were exactly the same for each period, representing 100% remittance of the amounts reflected in the table.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: PCSO presented its contributions to the National Treasury through taxes, dividends, and mandatory contributions for 2021 through the first semester of 2026. The presentation identified taxes as the largest share, followed by dividends of PHP9.93 billion and Universal Healthcare contributions of PHP9.53 billion, although the total five-year figure and tax figure were unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Attorney Lisa Enshong
thread.said: PCSO reported that total contributions increased from 14,560,000,000 in 2021 to 21,850,000,000 in 2025, described as a 50.1 increase.

thread.speaker: Attorney Anna Lisa
thread.said: PCSO stated that it had remitted an additional 11,060,000,000 as of 06/30/2026, bringing the total contributions reflected in the table to 112,350,000,000.

thread.speaker: Chair Mika Swan Singh
thread.said: The chair compared PCSO's sales trajectory with its taxes, dividends, and special-law remittances and asked why the upward trajectory in sales revenues was not matched by the trajectory of government contributions.

thread.speaker: Chair Mika Swan Singh
thread.said: The chair cited sales or net-receipt figures rising from 60,400,000,000 in 2023 to 61.3 in 2024, 63.8 in 2025, 65.9 in 2026, and 67.2 in 2027.

thread.speaker: Chair Mika Swan Singh
thread.said: The chair said total taxes, dividends, and other remittances appeared to be 22,900,000,000 in 2023, 22.26 in 2024, 21.85 in 2025, and 11 in the first half of 2026. She said she assumed the full-year 2026 amount would be 2,021,000,000,000; this figure is unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Chair Mika Swan Singh
thread.said: The chair asked why sales revenues were consistently increasing from 2023 to 2027 while taxes, dividends, and other remittances were not increasing at the same time.

thread.speaker: Johann, PCSO accounting and budget department
thread.said: Johann explained that taxes were primarily corporate income tax and that net income affected dividends as well. He also cited final income tax and tax on winnings, saying the tax on winnings depended on winnings above 20 or 10020%; the exact threshold was unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Johann, PCSO accounting and budget department
thread.said: Johann said other special contributions, including UHC, were affected by sales and that DST was also affected as sales increased. He summarized that taxes and dividends were principally affected by corporate income and final income taxes.

thread.speaker: Chair Mika Swan Singh
thread.said: The chair followed up on the downward trend in the Republic Acts and executive orders column, citing 108, six eighty in 2024, and three forty four in 2025, with the figures and their units unclear. She asked whether particular laws or executive orders caused the erratic trend in support for special laws.

thread.speaker: Johann, PCSO accounting and budget department
thread.said: Johann answered that the Republic Acts and executive orders category depended on sales, including contributions involving the Girl Scouts and Boy Scouts. He also cited the share from dangerous-drugs forfeited prizes; the detailed explanation was partly garbled.

thread.speaker: Chair Mika Swan Singh
thread.said: The chair said the trends were erratic because taxes, dividends, and Republic Acts and executive orders were contingent on factors that were not within PCSO's control, while UHC was a constant earmark under the law. She nevertheless expected contributions generally to rise with sales.

thread.speaker: Chair Mika Swan Singh
thread.said: The chair commended PCSO's contributions to the national government and cited roughly 112,000,000,000 pesos from 2021 to 2026 as an important source of funding for government programs and projects.
